title: ui: the console opens a record page scoped to the current app (`PageSchema.apps`), so an app can reach its own `sys_user` page (#28979 ruling A)
body:
domain:spec#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmPi25XXKx92Xmg4viS

Filing gate: ③ follow-up the ruling assigns. The director's ruling on #28979 (batch #453 item 1, letter A, maintainer 「同意」) binds a page-level app scope. The spec half landed in PR #29437 (`b16ee8ba06`, 2026-11-02 20:11Z), which closes #28979. The key is declared `[PLANNED — not yet rendered]` until the console reads it. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.
Reader: `domain:ui`, the console's record-page resolution (`usePageAssignment` in `ui/packages/app-shell`).

## What landed in spec

- `PageSchema.apps?: string[]` on a `type: 'record'` page bound to an object. The entries are app **names** (`AppSchema.name`), at least 1, unique.
- `defaultRecordPageObject(page, app?)` in `packages/spec/src/ui/default-record-page.ts` is the one reading of a slot. With `app` passed, it answers which object this page is the record page for inside that app. Without `app`, it reads the deployment default (`isDefault`).
- There is one page per object per app. The stack door, the registry door and the save door refuse a second one (`DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT`, carrying `app`).

## What the console must do

On a record route, resolve the page in this order:
1. Resolve the route's app segment to the app with `matchAppBySegment` (package id first, then name, already in the tree). Take the first page for which `defaultRecordPageObject(p, app.name) === objectName`.
2. Otherwise, use today's default read (`isDefault`).
3. Otherwise, use today's declaration order.

With no scoped page, every branch falls through to today's line.

⚠️ **Contract review flag ③.2 on #29437 (must get right).** The route segment is NOT the app name. `/apps/SEGMENT` is `appRouteSegment(app) = app._packageId ?? app.name` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/appRoute.ts`). So resolve the segment to the app, then pass `app.name`. Never compare the raw segment to `apps` entries.

A corner to pin: a package that ships two apps shares one package-id segment, and `matchAppBySegment` resolves that segment to the first app. The second app's scoped page is reachable only under its name segment, as the `appAddressSegment` docblock states.

## Done when

- **Pin 1 (the ruling's own).** The duly composition opens its scoped `sys_user` page (`duly_member`, `apps: ['duly']`) from People inside the Duly app. Setup → Users, under `/apps/com.objectstack.setup/...`, still opens plugin-auth's `sys_user_detail`.
- With no `apps` anywhere, resolution is byte-identical to today. The existing assignment tests stay green unchanged.
- The two-apps-one-package corner above is pinned.
- The spec liveness row for `page.apps` flips from `planned` to `live`, citing the console reader. The describe's `[PLANNED — not yet rendered]` marker and its closing "until the console reads it" sentence are removed in the same PR. That is the one spec edit this card owes.

Downstream: objectstack-ai/duly#113 tracks duly's URL-action stopgap. It can be deleted once this card lands.

Ruling-ref: #28979 batch #453 item 1 (A) · parent #28979 · key PR #29437.
